channel.title: Botany (2026) — Research Digest
channel.description: Recent curated links for Botany in 2026, including short summaries and source URLs.

item.title: Global functional shifts in trees driven by alien naturalization and native extinction
item.description: Research analyzing global tree assemblages shows that the naturalization of alien species and the extinction risk of natives are reshaping functional trait distributions in forests, with implications for ecosystem processes and resilience.

item.title: Genomic cradle for thousands
item.description: A perspective highlighting recent advances in large-scale plant genome sequencing, arguing that streamlined, high-throughput workflows and open data sharing can accelerate discoveries across evolutionary biology, systematics, and crop improvement.

item.title: Genome-wide analysis of DNA methylation in response to light and salt stress in a halophyte with single cell C4 pathway
item.description: Reports a genome-wide methylome survey of a single-cell C4 halophyte exposed to light and salinity, identifying differentially methylated regions and putative regulatory loci that modulate stress-responsive gene expression and adaptation.

item.title: Primed to fail: Primed acclimation to water stress can lead to greater disease severity and reduced yields in Sclerotium rolfsii-inoculated cultivated peanut (Arachis hypogaea L.)
item.description: Demonstrates that drought priming, while intended to boost tolerance, can inadvertently heighten Sclerotium rolfsii disease severity in peanut and depress yields, underscoring risks of priming under combined abiotic–biotic stress.

item.title: Applying plures contra Herculem. A commentary on ‘New intrageneric interactions in Macroptilium (Benth.)’
item.description: Places new findings on Macroptilium intrageneric interactions in a broader comparative and cytogenomic context, advocating multi-pronged approaches to disentangle complex evolutionary relationships within the genus.

item.title: Bracts and beyond – spikelet diversity in the wider Poales: a commentary on ‘Hygroscopic awns and inflorescence architecture in a wind-pollinated Australian monocot: functional convergence with grasses’
item.description: Synthesizes evidence on spikelet and bract diversity across Poales, discussing functional convergence of hygroscopic awns and inflorescence architecture between a non-grass monocot and grasses.

item.title: Elucidation of gene clusters underlying withanolide biosynthesis in ashwagandha through yeast metabolic engineering
item.description: Identifies and functionally validates key enzymes—four cytochrome P450s, a dehydrogenase and a sulfotransferase—that assemble the core scaffold of withanolides in ashwagandha, using yeast metabolic engineering to map the biosynthetic gene clusters.

item.title: Elucidation of gene clusters underlying withanolide biosynthesis in ashwagandha through yeast metabolic engineering
item.description: Identifies and functionally validates key enzyme-encoding gene clusters that assemble the core withanolide scaffold in ashwagandha, using yeast metabolic engineering; findings enable scalable production and pathway redesign of these medicinal metabolites.

item.title: Isolation leads to greater clonality and reduced seed production in a temperate seagrass
item.description: This study shows that population isolation in a temperate seagrass increases clonal reproduction while diminishing sexual reproduction and seed output. The findings suggest that reduced gene flow compromises reproductive capacity, with implications for conservation strategies and restoration planning in fragmented marine plant habitats.

item.title: Functional redundancy and differentiation of two homologous cell wall invertases GmCWI11 and GmCWI12 in soybean: modulating seed yield and quality via sugar metabolism
item.description: Accepted manuscript reporting how two homologous cell wall invertase genes in soybean show overlapping yet distinct roles in sugar partitioning, influencing seed yield and composition. The study links invertase activity to metabolic flux that underpins seed development and quality traits.

item.title: The Week in Botany January 19, 2026
item.description: Weekly roundup highlighting recent plant science, including a single-cell in planta screen for rapid gene function discovery and a new legume–pathogen model revealing components of quantitative root-rot resistance, plus community news and upcoming events.

item.title: Single-nucleus RNA-seq reveals apical-basal polarity as a somatic embryogenesis checkpoint in Picea abies
item.description: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing shows that apical–basal cell polarity controls a key checkpoint in Norway spruce somatic embryogenesis, identifies a polarity-linked transcription factor, and offers a resource to improve conifer clonal propagation.

item.title: ABA- and ET-induced systemic and intergenerational resistance against rice root-knot nematodes converges on OsOsMPK5-dependent signaling
item.description: Elevated abscisic acid and ethylene trigger a shared OsMPK5-dependent pathway that boosts rice defenses to root‑knot nematodes and passes this resistance to the next generation.

item.title: Early nodulin-like protein MtENODL29 inhibits nodule senescence in Medicago truncatula
item.description: An early nodulin-like protein, MtENODL29, delays legume root nodule senescence, sustaining nitrogen fixation and supporting plant growth in Medicago truncatula.

item.title: Proton channel inactivation results in loss of chloroplast NDH complex activity
item.description: Mutating proton‑motive residues in the NdhF subunit of photosynthetic complex I inactivates the chloroplast NDH complex, demonstrating tight coupling of proton and electron transfer.

item.title: Visualizing physical interactions between guard and epidermal cells during light-induced stomatal opening in two angiosperms
item.description: Live imaging reveals that even minimal light‑induced stomatal opening requires guard cells to laterally displace into neighboring epidermal cells, accompanied by epidermal cell shape changes.

item.title: Functional redundancy and differentiation of two homologous cell wall invertases GmCWI11 and GmCWI12 in soybean: modulating seed yield and quality via sugar metabolism
item.description: Researchers dissect the roles of two homologous cell wall invertases in soybean and show both overlap and specialization in sugar metabolism during seed development. Tuning GmCWI11/12 activity alters assimilate partitioning, with measurable effects on seed filling, yield, and quality, pointing to breeding and gene-editing targets.

item.title: Growth-defense trade-off defines a diffusion limit: a commentary on ‘Boundary-line trade-off in bryophytes between UV photoprotection and photosynthetic capacity, but not desiccation tolerance’
item.description: This commentary discusses new evidence for a fundamental trade-off in bryophytes: investing in UV photoprotection reduces potential photosynthetic capacity. The authors frame the results as a diffusion-limited growth–defense balance, highlighting implications for how non-vascular plants adapt to high-UV environments.

item.title: Decline in botanical education threatens response to climate action and food security
item.description: An international survey of 421 plant scientists finds that shortages in botanical training and expertise risk undermining biodiversity conservation, climate action, and sustainable agriculture. The study emphasizes the importance of early hands-on experiences and mentorship to attract students and calls for stronger plant-science curricula and outreach.

item.title: Scientists Are Rethinking Bamboo as a Powerful New Superfood
item.description: A comprehensive review synthesizes laboratory and human studies indicating bamboo shoots contain bioactive compounds that may support glycemic control, cardiovascular and gut health, and reduce inflammation and oxidative stress. The authors call for standardized preparations and more clinical trials to validate health claims.

item.title: 2026 in paleobotany
item.description: Continuously updated overview of 2026 paleobotany research and discoveries, cataloguing newly described fossil plant taxa and notable studies (e.g., algae responses across geologic events and vegetation shifts in the Triassic–Jurassic), with references to the academic literature.

item.title: Upcoming and open special issues | Journal of Experimental Botany
item.description: Journal announcement page listing current special‑issue themes relevant to botany (e.g., single‑cell/spatial transcriptomics in plants, plant phenomics and enviromics, AI‑driven plant research), providing scope notes and deadlines for submissions.

item.title: Latest updates from the New Phytologist Foundation | January 2026
item.description: Monthly roundup announcing the 2025 Tansley Medal winner, highlighting a new Anthromes and terrestrial carbon special collection across New Phytologist and Plants, People, Planet, and sharing early details for upcoming symposia on plant mating systems and domestication.

item.title: New Phytologist and Plants, People, Planet in the news in 2025
item.description: A curated look at plant-science studies from the foundation’s journals that drew notable media attention in 2025, spanning topics from pollination and plant–insect interactions to crop-related genetics, with guidance for authors planning press releases.

item.title: Beat the Rush: Order These 9 In-Demand Flower and Veg Seeds in January Before They Sell Out Everywhere
item.description: Roundup of nine high-demand flower and vegetable seeds expected to sell out quickly this season, with notes on limited-run collections and heritage varieties; urges early ordering and provides brief cultivation highlights.

item.title: These 12 garden trends are set to reshape our outdoor spaces in 2026 - from climate-resilient planting to foraging gardens
item.description: Overview of 2026 gardening trends emphasizing climate-resilient planting, wildlife-friendly practices, water conservation, upcycling, and edible/foraging gardens, with practical examples and plant suggestions.

item.title: January 2026 Virtual Symposium
item.description: Announcement of a wildlife gardening research symposium highlighting evidence-based practices for nature-friendly gardens, including sessions on winter garden management and biodiversity support.

item.title: Ficus Named Cult-Favorite Houseplants of 2026 by Industry Experts - And No, We're Not Just Talking About Fiddle Leaf Figs
item.description: Industry feature naming 2026 as the 'Year of the Ficus,' outlining popular Ficus species for indoor use, care guidance (light, humidity, cleaning), and reasons for their resurgence among houseplant enthusiasts.

item.title: IPTG- and estradiol-inducible gene expression systems in the unicellular red alga Cyanidioschyzon merolae
item.description: Research article describing controllable inducible systems for gene expression in the red alga Cyanidioschyzon merolae, enabling precise modulation of protein levels to study photosynthetic eukaryotes.

item.title: Transcriptome profiling reveals divergent response strategies in two olive cultivars with contrasting drought tolerance
item.description: Comparative transcriptome analyses of two olive cultivars uncovered distinct drought-response strategies, with the tolerant cultivar showing early metabolic control that maintains cellular function, offering targets for crop improvement.

item.title: Plant These 7 Perennials in January and Your Garden Will Be Buzzing With Pollinators Come Spring
item.description: A practical guide recommending seven pollinator-friendly perennials (e.g., yarrow, coneflower, sedum) to plant as bare roots in January, with tips to boost biodiversity and garden success.

item.title: 5 flower seeds to sow in January for a colorful summer garden
item.description: Recommendations for five flowers (including snapdragons, petunias, dianthus) to start from seed in January, outlining ease of growth, seasonal care, and pollinator benefits.

item.title: Bewitching the host: Striga disrupts host stomatal ABA signaling by impairing the tryptophan lock
item.description: An Insight article discussing how the parasitic plant Striga manipulates the abscisic acid (ABA) signaling pathway in host plants by targeting the receptor 'tryptophan lock' mechanism. The commentary synthesizes new findings showing that a Striga protein phosphatase perturbs host stomatal responses, highlighting implications for crop protection against parasitic weeds.

item.title: Evolutionary and functional significance of ShPP2C1 in the parasitic life strategy of Striga
item.description: This research characterizes the Striga protein phosphatase ShPP2C1 and shows how it modulates ABA signaling to aid parasitism. Comparative analyses and functional assays link ShPP2C1 to suppression of host defenses and altered stomatal regulation, suggesting a potential target for mitigating Striga damage in crops.

item.title: Genetic and evolutionary insights into the GoP1 gene, which regulates yellow pollen coloration and enhances pollinator attraction in cotton
item.description: A research article reporting genetic and evolutionary analyses of the GoP1 gene controlling yellow pollen coloration in cotton. The study links pigment phenotype to increased pollinator attraction, illustrating how floral trait genetics can influence plant–pollinator interactions with potential applications in crop breeding.

item.title: Transcriptome profiling reveals divergent response strategies in two olive cultivars with contrasting drought tolerance
item.description: Comparative transcriptomics of drought-tolerant and -sensitive olive cultivars shows early metabolic control and stress-mitigation pathways underlying superior tolerance, offering targets for crop improvement.

item.title: Transcriptome profiling reveals divergent response strategies in two olive cultivars with contrasting drought tolerance
item.description: RNA-seq across drought treatments shows that drought-tolerant and drought-sensitive olive cultivars deploy distinct molecular strategies, with early metabolic control linked to maintaining cellular function and informing breeding for resilience.

item.title: Phosphorylation of GhSKD1 by GhCIPK6D1 regulates potassium efflux during the drought response in cotton
item.description: The study identifies a GhCIPK6D1–GhSKD1 phosphorylation module that limits K+ efflux under drought, thereby negatively regulating cotton drought tolerance and highlighting a signaling node for improving stress resilience.

item.title: CitNOR-like1 is conserved in the regulation of ascorbic acid accumulation in plants
item.description: A NAC transcription factor, CitNOR-like1, suppresses ascorbic acid by repressing a key biosynthetic gene, suggesting a conserved mechanism shaping vitamin C levels and crop nutritional quality.

item.title: BnaMYB52 negatively regulates drought resistance by controlling stomatal and non-stomatal water loss in Brassica napus
item.description: BnaMYB52 targets multiple regulators, including BnaMYB96, BnaMYB30 and BnaMYC2, to modulate both stomatal and cuticular water loss, thereby reducing drought resistance in oilseed rape.

item.title: A Comprehensive Database of Leaf Temperature, Water, and CO2 Fluxes in Young Oil Palm Plants Across Diverse Climate Scenarios
item.description: Researchers present a high-resolution dataset linking 3D plant architecture with leaf- and plant-scale gas exchange across controlled CO2, light, temperature, and humidity scenarios to improve parameterization and evaluation of functional–structural plant models.

item.title: Drought stress increases total C released from roots
item.description: Reports that drought stress increases the total amount of carbon released from plant roots into soils, highlighting implications for rhizosphere processes and soil carbon cycling.

item.title: Throwing away to survive: rhizome senescence as a strategy adopted by a herbaceous clonal plant to remain young forever
item.description: Shows that programmed senescence of aging rhizomes in a clonal herbaceous plant helps maintain vigor by discarding older modules, offering an adaptive strategy for longevity.

item.title: Coordinated brassinosteroid and auxin signaling modulates ray floret ligule and leaf morphology in Gerbera hybrida
item.description: Demonstrates that balanced brassinosteroid–auxin signaling is essential to achieve proper size and flatness of petals and leaves in Gerbera, illuminating hormonal crosstalk in organ shape.

item.title: Fly-arousing orchid and zombie fungus among 2025 botanical and fungal finds
item.description: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew and partners report 2,025 newly named plant and fungal species from 2025, including a spider-parasitizing “zombie” fungus and a fly-mimicking orchid. The piece highlights biodiversity gains alongside extinction risks and the urgency of taxonomy and conservation.

item.title: Botany January Update 2026
item.description: A field report from Jersey’s Botany Section recounts their New Year Plant Hunt, logging 88 species in flower despite winter conditions. Notable observations included unseasonal blooms such as Pilosella peletariana and common winter-flowering species like Bellis perennis and Cymbalaria muralis.

item.title: Meet the unexpected 'it' flower of 2026 - why lantana is set to be this year's garden border hero
item.description: Lantana is touted as a 2026 standout for UK gardens thanks to vivid blooms, drought tolerance, and long flowering seasons. The article frames its rise within shifting climates and practical care tips for container growing and overwintering.

item.title: The Week in Botany — January 5, 2026
item.description: A curated roundup of recent plant science news and papers, including notes on newly declared extinctions, deforestation policy impacts, and highlights of research such as conserved patterning mechanisms in liverworts and resources for improving lab culture.

item.title: When stress drives you to kidnap: RACK1A sequesters FSD1 into stress granules during salt stress
item.description: A news-and-views piece summarizing findings that RACK1A relocates FSD1 into stress granules under salt stress, highlighting a mechanism of stress response organization in plants.

item.title: Call for Papers for Upcoming Focus Collections in Plant Physiology (2026)
item.description: Announces 2026 Focus Collections on early land plant evolution, light, and algae/aquatic plants, outlining themes and timelines relevant to current plant science research.

item.title: Winter blooming of hundreds of plants in UK ‘visible signal’ of climate breakdown
item.description: Analysis of nine years of New Year’s Plant Hunt data shows that for every 1°C rise in temperatures during November–December, an additional ~2.5 species are observed flowering at New Year. In 2025, 310 native species (646 including non-natives) were recorded in bloom, far above historical expectations, highlighting how warming winters are disrupting plant phenology and ecosystems.

item.title: From growth to survival: Aux/IAA genes in plant development and stress management
item.description: A review of the Aux/IAA transcriptional repressors detailing how they integrate auxin signals to control organ patterning, growth, and adaptive responses. The authors synthesize recent genetic and molecular findings and outline how Aux/IAA networks modulate stress tolerance.
